source.title: People v Louree (2007 NY Slip Op 04679)

captionLines: The People of the State of New York, Respondent,

qualifierLines: {**8 NY3d at 542} OPINION OF THE COURT

Because I believe that defendant was required to preserve the issue for appellate review, I respectfully dissent. The record reveals that defendant was made aware of the postrelease component of his sentence at the sentencing proceeding (, 4 NY3d 242, 245 [2005]). Thus, defendant was required to preserve the issue as nothing in this case calls for the "rare case" exception to the preservation doctrine described in People v Lopez (71 NY2d 662, 666 [1988]). Here, defendant could have raised an objection to the sentencing judge and he would have then been able to raise the issue on his direct appeal (, 30 AD3d 961 [4th Dept 2006], lv denied 7 NY3d 789 [2006]).
Accordingly, I dissent and would affirm the order of the Appellate Division.{**8 NY3d at 547}
